profile_md: Berkeley's documented employer-linked group project routes are distributed across graduate schools rather than institution-wide. The Goldman School's Introduction to Policy Analysis (S1) places teams of four to six first-year MPP students with public-sector agencies and NGOs, producing a report and presentation (Spring 2027 call open). Engineering's MEng Capstone (S2) runs nine-month teams of three to five on industry-proposed projects, but the page also describes faculty-involved projects, so external sponsorship across all teams is unproven. Data Science Discovery (S3) offers mentor-set projects with teams of 1-5, partly academic mentors, so group and employer criteria are unclear. Haas offers Social Sector Solutions (nonprofit client teams of 5-7), Haas@Work (firm challenges) and Startup Lab, all MBA or graduate-led with weak current-year evidence. The legacy Berkeley Discovery framework is a platform, not a scheme. No undergraduate curricular route meeting all three criteria was verified; participation is optional or programme-specific, with no institution-wide route found. No participation numbers were located.
gaps: Undergraduate humanities/social science and EECS/Data Science routes not searched (limit). Current-year evidence absent for most Haas routes. Compulsory status of IPA and MEng capstone unconfirmed. Further departmental capstones likely exist.
